niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
engine_stated_criteria: Udemy — *Do Your Own Shadow Work: Beginning to Advanced Practices
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want a psychology-oriented approach, a particular spiritual tradition, or a practical daily routine. These are promising places to start:

### Shadow work
- **Jung Platform — *Engage the Shadow***: A structured, Jungian-oriented option with video and audio lessons and practical exercises. A good fit if you want depth psychology rather than a quick set of journaling prompts. [Course details](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)
- **Udemy — *Shadow Work Course and Workbook***: A lower-cost, self-paced introduction with a workbook. Check the current syllabus and instructor background, and treat it as educational material rather than therapy. [Course details](https://www.udemy.com/course/shadow-work-course/)
- **Udemy — *Do Your Own Shadow Work: Beginning to Advanced Practices***: Another self-paced option that advertises a range of exercises. Review the course outline carefully to see whether its approach matches yours. [Course details](https://www.udemy.com/course/shadow-work-x/)

### Spiritual practice
- **Center for Action and Contemplation — *Essentials of Engaged Contemplation***: A fully online course for people interested in contemplative practice within a Christian tradition. [Course details](https://cac.org/living-school/essentials-of-engaged-contemplation-course/)
- **World Community for Christian Meditation — *An Introduction to Christian Meditation***: A six-week course focused on establishing a regular meditation practice, especially suitable if you want a clearly defined tradition and routine. [Course details](https://wccm.org/courses/)
- **Spirituality & Practice — online courses and retreats**: A broad directory of self-paced courses and practice circles, useful if you want to compare approaches across traditions. [Course directory](https://www.spiritualityandpractice.com/ecourses/course)

**How to choose:** For shadow work, I’d start with Jung Platform if you want a more substantial, psychology-informed course; choose a self-paced course if you mainly want guided exercises. For spiritual practice, pick a course whose tradition and daily practices genuinely appeal to you—consistency matters more than finding a supposedly universal method.

A note of care: shadow work can bring up painful memories or intense emotions. It isn’t a substitute for mental-health care; if you have a trauma history or feel overwhelmed, consider working with a licensed therapist and pause exercises that feel destabilizing.
